Body: The success path returns `{ mcpClient, status, instructions }` but the early-return failure/disabled paths (e.g. `{ mcpClient: undefined, status: { status: "disabled" } }`) don't include an `instructions` field. The callers use `if (result.instructions)` which handles `undefined` correctly, but adding `instructions: undefined` to the failure paths would make the return type union explicit and consistent.

ref={root}` will not assign the DOM element to the `root` variable in Solid. As a result, `if (root) obs.observe(root)` often won’t observe anything and the component will only become ready via the timeout, undermining the IntersectionObserver-based deferral. Use a ref callback to assign the element (e.g., set `root` from the element parameter).

Initializing `ready` based on `typeof window` can cause SSR hydration mismatch/flicker: server render will show the real part (`ready` true), but the client initial render will show the placeholder (`ready` false) until the observer/timeout runs. If this code path is used with SSR/hydration, consider initializing `ready` consistently across server+client during hydration (e.g., treat the hydration phase like SSR) so the initial markup matches.
```suggestion
  const [ready, setReady] = createSignal(false)
```

`readdir()` on `node_modules/.bin` can return multiple shim files (e.g. `foo.cmd`, `foo.ps1`, `foo`), and the directory entry order is not guaranteed. Picking `[0]` risks returning a non-executable shim on Windows (notably `.ps1`) or otherwise being nondeterministic. Consider selecting the binary deterministically (e.g. on win32 prefer `*.cmd`, otherwise prefer the no-extension entry; and/or filter out `.ps1`). This same selection logic should apply to both the `retry` and `files` paths (see similar `.cmd` handling in `lsp/server.ts`).

Consider capturing the previous value before overwriting it and restoring it on stop (restore previous string if defined, else delete).

`await prompt.click()` does not guarantee the terminal’s delayed focus retries have finished (the terminal panel re-focuses via RAF and setTimeout(120/240ms)), so the next `prompt.fill()`/slash popover assertion may still race under load. Consider explicitly waiting for the terminal to take focus (e.g., expect the terminal textarea to be focused) and then re-focusing the prompt and asserting `prompt` is focused before the second `/terminal` cycle.
```suggestion
  await expect(terminal).toBeVisible()

  // Wait for the terminal textarea to take focus, then re-focus the prompt
  const terminalTextarea = terminal.locator("textarea")
  await expect(terminalTextarea).toBeFocused()
  await prompt.click()
  await expect(prompt).toBeFocused()
```

`root` is resolved as `../..` from `src/renderer`, which points to `packages/desktop-electron/src`. That makes `join(root, "electron.vite.config.ts")` look for `src/electron.vite.config.ts` (doesn't exist) and also causes `resolve(root, rendererRoot, pub)` to duplicate `src` in the path. Adjust the base directory so it points at `packages/desktop-electron` (e.g., walk up one more level or resolve from `import.meta.url` to the package root) before reading the config and resolving `publicDir`.
```suggestion
const root = resolve(dir, "../../..")
```

The `Show` condition hides the font preload `<Link>` tags whenever `location` is undefined. In SSR contexts (e.g. SolidStart apps consuming `@opencode-ai/ui/font`), `location` is undefined on the server, so this change drops the preload tags entirely from the server-rendered HTML and can regress initial font loading performance on the web. Consider defaulting to rendering preloads when `location` is undefined (and only skipping when `location.protocol === "file:"`), or deriving the protocol from the server request when SSR is in use.
```suggestion
      <Show when={typeof location === "undefined" || location.protocol !== "file:"}>
```

Potential bug: `resource` could be `undefined` if neither `provider.options?.resourceName` nor `AZURE_RESOURCE_NAME` env var is set. When `vars()` returns this undefined value and it gets used in `url.replaceAll(field, value)`, it will replace the placeholder with the literal string `"undefined"`. Consider either filtering out undefined values before replacement, or returning an empty object from `vars()` when resource is undefined.

The e2e driver appends all terminal output into `received`/`rendered` with no cap. In longer sessions or noisy terminals this can grow without bound and increase memory use (and make `includes()` checks slower). Consider storing only a tail window (e.g., last N chars) and/or tracking counts/sequence numbers instead of full buffers.

`terminalState()` returns the full driver object (including potentially large `received`/`rendered` strings) across the Playwright boundary on every poll. This can become a performance bottleneck and increase flakiness as output grows. Consider evaluating the readiness/contains checks in the page context and returning only booleans/small primitives (or expose a helper that returns only the needed fields).

This removes the previous canonicalization (`Filesystem.resolve(...)`) of the `directory` input. Passing a non-resolved/relative path into `Instance.provide({ directory })` can change behavior (and can be risky if callers can influence this value). Prefer restoring canonicalization (e.g., `Filesystem.resolve(decoded)` or `path.resolve(decoded)`) so the server always operates on a normalized absolute directory.

Commenting out the `Disallow` rules makes share/session pages crawlable. If shares may contain sensitive content, this can lead to unintended indexing and distribution. Consider keeping these disallowed by default (or add a clear policy + per-share `noindex` controls if indexing is desired).

Disallow: /share/

`AsyncStorage.clear()` clears `pending` and then clears the underlying store, but it does not coordinate with an in-flight `flush()`. If a `flush()` is already running (it copies a batch and then writes it), `clear()` can run concurrently and the flush may re-populate the store after it was cleared. Consider cancelling any scheduled timer and awaiting the current `flushing`/`flush()` completion before clearing the store (and/or using a shared lock) so `clearCache` reliably removes persisted state.

Use the standard conditional expression pattern used elsewhere in this repo (e.g. `cond && a || b` in `.github/workflows/deploy.yml:38`) to select between the dev-specific group and the shared group.

The `typeperf` process is spawned without `windowsHide: true`. Per codebase convention (see `packages/opencode/src/util/process.ts:55-60` and `packages/desktop-electron/src/main/cli.ts:148-153`), Windows subprocesses should set `windowsHide: true` to avoid flashing console windows.

`Agent.resolveModel` can return the parent session model as a fallback, but the parent model passed in here drops `msg.info.variant`. Since assistant messages include `variant`, this causes subagent Tasks to lose the parent session's reasoning mode whenever tiers aren’t configured. Pass `variant: msg.info.variant` into the `parentSessionModel` argument so the fallback preserves variant too.

The example Task invocations here omit `subagent_type`, but this tool requires `subagent_type` (and the text above explicitly says it must be specified). Update the example to include a concrete `subagent_type` so it’s copy/pasteable and not misleading.

The per-agent `model_tiers.*.model` fields are defined as plain `z.string()`. Elsewhere in config, model strings use the shared `ModelId` schema (for consistent schema refs/docs and to keep the intended provider/model format documented). Consider switching these tier model fields to `ModelId` (and/or reusing a shared tier schema) to keep config validation/docs consistent.

Same as agent config: the global `model_tiers.*.model` fields are plain `z.string()`, while other model fields use `ModelId` for consistent schema refs/docs. Using `ModelId` here (or a shared tier schema) would keep validation/documentation consistent across config fields.

`item.modelTiers` is populated from a `Partial<Record<...>>`, but it’s then cast to a full `Record<...>`. This cast can mask missing tiers at the type level and makes it easier to accidentally assume all tiers exist later. Prefer keeping the partial type (or the explicit `{ quick?: ...; standard?: ...; advanced?: ... }` shape) and avoid the `as Record<...>` assertion.

The composer probe effect runs unconditionally and tracks `store.collapsed`, `off()` (spring-driven), and `props.todos`, so it will re-run frequently (e.g., every animation frame during collapse/open) and allocate `states: props.todos.map(...)` even when the e2e composer driver is not enabled in normal app usage. Consider gating this effect behind a cheap `__opencode_e2e?.composer?.enabled` check (before reading reactive values) so it becomes a no-op with no reactive subscriptions outside e2e runs.

Inside the new e2e-driver `createEffect`, the local helper function is named `sync`, which shadows the outer `sync` variable from `useSync()`. This makes the code harder to follow and increases the risk of accidental misuse during future edits. Rename the inner function to something like `syncTestState` (or similar) to avoid the shadowing.

This effect registers a global `window` event listener for `composerEvent` whenever a session id is present, even when the e2e composer driver is not enabled (i.e., `window.__opencode_e2e?.composer?.enabled` is falsy in normal runtime). To avoid unnecessary global listeners in production, consider checking the enabled flag and returning early before adding the listener.

This test relies on a fixed `await sleep(50)` to wait for the async log write to land on disk. In `Log.create().info()`, the write is not awaited (it can be async after `Log.init()`), so a fixed delay can be flaky under load/CI and cause intermittent failures.

Consider replacing the fixed sleep with a small retry loop (poll the log file until the matching line appears or a timeout elapses), similar to the `wait()` pattern used in other tests (e.g. `packages/opencode/test/pty/pty-session.test.ts`).

`Filesystem.resolve(match)` can throw for non-ENOENT errors (e.g. EACCES, ELOOP on problematic symlinks). If that happens inside `addSkill`, the rejection will bubble up and can cause the whole scan to fail (e.g. `Promise.all(matches.map(addSkill))`), skipping all remaining skills. Consider wrapping the resolve call in a try/catch and treating failures like a per-skill load error (log + return) so a single bad path can’t abort discovery.

This PR changes the ordering of `store.session` away from being strictly id-sorted (e.g., sessions are now kept in “most recently updated” order). There is still code that uses `Binary.search(..., (s) => s.id)` against the session list (which requires id-sorted input) — for example `packages/app/src/components/prompt-input/submit.ts:270-281` upserts into the global session list via `Binary.search`. That binary search will return incorrect indices / miss existing items once the list is no longer id-sorted, potentially creating duplicates or corrupting ordering. Please replace remaining `Binary.search` usages over `Session[]` with a linear lookup (`findIndex`) or an insertion strategy consistent with the new recency ordering (e.g., using `compareSessionRecent`) and ensure the session list invariant is consistent everywhere.

`sortedRootSessions` no longer uses the `now` value (it’s renamed to `_now`) since sorting is no longer time-window dependent. Consider removing this parameter entirely and updating call sites (`layout.tsx`, `sidebar-*.tsx`, tests) to avoid carrying an unused argument and to make the helper’s contract clearer.

If the repository doesn't have the `size:*` labels created yet, `issues.addLabels` will fail and the entire workflow run will be marked as failed. The nested ternary used to compute `next` is difficult to scan and easy to mis-edit when thresholds change. Switching to a small helper (e.g., ordered threshold table + loop, or straightforward if/else chain) would make this easier to maintain.
